BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

Of course. Here is my detailed review of the Seller's documents against the Wattlebridge Holdings Buyer Negotiation Playbook for Project Kestrel, followed by a summary of recommendations.

### Executive Summary

The Seller's draft represents a significant departure from our playbook in almost every material respect. Their strategy is to collapse all liability into a single, restrictive "general regime" with low caps, high thresholds, short time limits, and broad exclusions. This directly undermines our core positions on fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, and disclosure standards. The draft also attempts to shift risk to us through broad buyer-knowledge exclusions and deemed disclosure. Every specific risk area identified in our diligence (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, employee bonuses) is either downplayed, deferred, or excluded from the funds flow.

---

### Detailed Analysis: Departures from the Playbook & Reasoning for Pushback

#### 1. General Liability Cap (Clause 12.1)
*   **Seller's Position:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap.
*   **Playbook Position:** Starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% cap is a conditional fallback **only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost**, which has not been given.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** This is a direct attempt to secure the fallback position without meeting the necessary internal approval condition. We must reject this outright and insist on the 25% / AUD 6,000,000 starting point. There is no justification for the lower cap based on the diligence performed.

#### 2. Thresholds & Basket (Clause 12.2)
*   **Seller's Position:** De minimis of AUD 25,000; basket of AUD 250,000, with recovery only for the **excess** above the basket.
*   **Playbook Position:** De minimis of AUD 5,000; aggregate basket of AUD 50,000, with seller liable **from the first dollar** once the basket is exceeded.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** The Seller's proposal is commercially unreasonable. A AUD 250,000 basket means we cannot recover the first AUD 250,000 of claims, which could easily swallow several smaller but significant warranty breaches. The "excess only" structure further disadvantages us. We must hold firm to our position: a low de minimis (AUD 5,000) and a "first dollar" liability once the AUD 50,000 basket is exceeded.

#### 3. Time Limits & Application to All Claims (Clauses 12.3 / 13)
*   **Seller's Position:** 18-month general claims period. Proposes that all claims (including fundamental/title) are subject to this short period unless stated otherwise.
*   **Playbook Position:** 24-month general claims period (18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's approval). Fundamental/Title claims require a separate regime with a **100% cap and a minimum six-year period**, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** This is a critical attack on our risk allocation. The Seller is trying to apply the short, restrictive general warranty regime to fundamental matters like title, capacity, and tax. A 18-month limit for title is completely unacceptable; we need at least six years to ensure the shares are legally ours and the company is solvent. We must insist on a separate, more robust regime for fundamental warranties.

#### 4. Limitations, Exclusive Remedy & Non-Reliance (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
*   **Seller's Position:** These provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**.
*   **Playbook Position:** Fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct must be **carved out** of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies, and non-reliance clauses to the maximum extent enforceable.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** Accepting the Seller's wording would mean that even if they committed fraud, their liability would be capped and time-barred. This is a non-negotiable point for us. We must ensure explicit carve-outs for fraud and wilful misconduct. No one may waive this protection.

#### 5. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1], [1.2])
*   **Seller's Position:** Relies on "general disclosure of the data room and public registers" as deemed disclosure.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **specific fair disclosure**; reject whole-data-room, public-register, or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** The Seller's approach is designed to avoid pinpoint responsibility for specific risks. By claiming the data room is general disclosure, they argue we had knowledge of everything and cannot claim surprise. We must reject this entirely. We require a Disclosure Letter that specifically lists known risks, liabilities, and exceptions from the warranties. General data room disclosure cannot be used to cure specific breaches of warranty.

#### 6. Buyer Knowledge (Clause 8.3)
*   **Seller's Position:** Blanket exclusion for any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including matters "discoverable" from the data room.
*   **Playbook Position:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud, or a specific indemnity.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** This is another attempt to use the data room to defeat our claims. It effectively makes our due diligence a double-edged sword: the more we find, the more they can argue we "knew" about it and thus cannot claim. We must delete this clause. If a knowledge qualifier is necessary, it must be narrowly drafted to refer only to actual, specific knowledge of named individuals at the Seller, not constructive knowledge from our own research.

#### 7. Bluefen Consent (Clause 3 / 6.3 / Disclosure Letter [2])
*   **Seller's Position:** "Reasonable endeavours" to obtain consent, with consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** Bluefen represents ~30% of revenue. "Reasonable endeavours" is too weak. We need a **condition precedent**: the Seller must deliver *effective, unconditional* written consent, with evidence that all its pre-conditions (e.g., under clause 11.3) are met, *before* we complete the transaction. Consent cannot be a post-completion obligation.

#### 8. Riverlark Facility (Clause 2 / 7 / Disclosure Letter [3])
*   **Seller's Position:** Release to be provided "following Completion."
*   **Playbook Position:** Require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** A post-completion release is unacceptable for a ~AUD 3.2M debt. This shifts all risk to us. We must require the Riverlark facility to be repaid in full **from the Completion funds at settlement**, with all security released simultaneously. The completion funds flow must reflect this direct repayment.

#### 9. Employee Bonuses (Funds Flow / Disclosure Letter [5])
*   **Seller's Position:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.
*   **Playbook Position:** DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** If these are genuine liabilities that must be paid upon completion, they must be accounted for in the price mechanism. If the Seller is paying them, that must be explicitly stated and funded. We cannot allow them to be a post-completion obligation of the company we are buying. They must be either deducted from the purchase price or explicitly funded by the Seller outside the funds flow.

#### 10. Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1 / Disclosure Letter [4])
*   **Seller's Position:** Indemnity is "limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate."
*   **Playbook Position:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** The Seller is trying to limit its liability to a specific payment amount, ignoring the broader IP transfer and warranty obligations. We need an indemnity that covers the full scope of the Ironquay matter, including the transfer of materials and representations. The fact that AUD 180,000 is "open" is a red flag that requires a broader, not narrower, indemnity.

#### 11. Export/Privacy Incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / Disclosure Letter [6])
*   **Seller's Position:** Characterized as a "preliminary operational matter" and "not expected to be material."
*   **Playbook Position:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** We should not accept the Seller's characterization. This is a potential data breach with significant regulatory and reputational risk. We must require the Seller to: (a) preserve all relevant logs and evidence, (b) conduct a thorough investigation and provide us with regular updates, and (c) warrant that as of completion, there is no confirmed breach, harm, or regulatory notification requirement arising from the incident. We cannot assume it is immaterial.

#### 12. Sandbar Renewals (Disclosure Letter [8])
*   **Seller's Position:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
*   **Playbook Position:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** We should not automatically accept this classification. We need to review the contracts (DD-008, DD-011) to confirm these are indeed ordinary-course, unavoidable costs and not extraordinary commitments or liabilities that should be addressed separately (e.g., as a debt or a specific indemnity).

#### 13. Title (Disclosure Letter [10])
*   **Seller's Position:** Title is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.
*   **Playbook Position:** Require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
*   **Reasoning for Pushback:** The share register is an internal document. It is not independent proof of title. We must require the Seller to provide independent evidence, such as a recent title search or a share transfer form, to confirm clean title to the shares.

---

### Summary of Recommendations

1.  **Reject the General Regime:** Do not accept the Seller's attempt to apply a single, restrictive set of rules to all claims. We must insist on separate regimes for General, Fundamental, and Title warranties as per our playbook.
2.  **Hold Firm on Caps and Thresholds:** Reject the 20% cap and the high basket/de minimis. Insist on 25% / AUD 6,000,000 cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, and a AUD 50,000 basket with first-dollar liability.
3.  **Insist on Fundamental Warranty Protections:** Ensure Title, Capacity, and Tax warranties have a 100% cap and a minimum six-year claim period, completely separate from the general basket and thresholds.
4.  **Carve Out Fraud and Misconduct:** This is non-negotiable. Explicitly carve out fraud, wilful concealment, and deliberate misconduct from all limitations.
5.  **Reject Deemed Disclosure:** Demand a specific Disclosure Letter that lists known risks. Reject any reliance on the data room or public records as a general defense.
6.  **Delete Blanket Buyer-Knowledge Exclusion:** If a knowledge qualifier is included, it must be narrow and based on actual knowledge of named individuals.
7.  **Make Key Consents and Releases Conditions Precedent:**
    *   **Bluefen:** Effective, unconditional consent must be delivered *before* completion.
    *   **Riverlark:** The facility must be repaid from completion funds, with security released at settlement.
8.  **Fix the Funds Flow:** Ensure the Employee Bonuses (AUD 420,000 + on-costs) are explicitly accounted for, either as a deduction from the price or a seller-funded obligation.
9.  **Strengthen Specific Indemnities:** Broaden the Ironquay IP indemnity and require a robust process for the Export/Privacy incident, including warranties that it is not a confirmed breach.
10. **Verify Title Independently:** Do not rely solely on the share register. Require independent title evidence.
11. **Escalate to Amelia Frost:** Any fallback positions (e.g., 20% cap, 18-month general period) require her prior written authority, which has not been given. Our response must reflect that these are not currently approved positions.
